craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of containment — the Vijñānavāda opponent staged at full strength, then held; śāstra-hammer couplets, negation-anaphora, terminal doctrine words. Opponent certainty in Vijñānavāda voice; correlative yathā/evam → As/so balance (row 3); end-weight niścayaḥ. Rejected: (a) softening double negation → killed by naiva/nāsty: the proof needs the opponent strong. (b) quatrain split → killed: certainty is one breath. Read aloud: AS-real AND-un-REAL CARR-y NO-mark … THIS-stands CER-tain.

lines: As real and unreal carry no mark between them, in own self —
so inert and non-inert carry none. This stands certain.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yathā sadasatām naiva viśeṣo 'sti nijātmani jadājaḍānām apy evaṃ nāsty asāv iti niścayaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What in things themselves distinguishes real from unreal, conscious from unconscious? → The opponent's opening certainty: distinctions have no seat in things themselves.
c1_essence: Every candidate seat of distinction — predicates, objecthood, conceded difference, free-standing being, function — collapses into knower-dependence; the opponent's no-difference is granted, then outflanked from inside (vv1-8).
Grasping-less awareness is declared inert, and the proof turns: only self-reflective consciousness can stand as ground (v9).
